title: Preserve actor decisions and distinct concern identity rules
statement: The Operational record persistence Module shall enforce the applicable prior-state preservation rules without altering actor-supplied meaning or treating engineering observations as structural approval, while distinguishing current Review finding identity from immutable change-blocker origin.

what.problem: A structurally shaped replacement can erase a finding, rewrite a blocker's original basis, or silently turn a mechanical observation into a new assessment.
what.desired_outcome: Explicit corrections remain possible while retained concern identity, original blocker basis, and actor-owned decisions stay attributable.

why.rationale: SR-042 separates structural validity from judgment and requires different preservation rules for findings and blockers; MOD-011 owns the prior/candidate comparison.

stakeholders: Engineers and agents supplying explicit command requests
Maintainers of MOD-011 and its Interface consumers

conditions: A candidate changes assessments, explanation values, findings, or blockers, or contains failed evidence, completed activity, or historical subject drift.

contexts: IF-003 validation against the coherent prior records and complete candidate for the same selected change.

how.approach: Compare only the preservation invariants applicable to the declared operation, retaining supplied decisions and separating recorded assertions from current mechanical observations.

how_much.scope: Actor-supplied subjects, applicability, narrative, provenance, status, decisions, finding IDs, blocker origin, and conditional Verify basis under the retained v3 contract.

acceptance_criteria: Actor-supplied status, subjects, applicability, provenance, explanation collection order and multiline meaning survive validation unchanged; neither a renderer nor validation creates another authoritative report.

Existing Review finding IDs cannot be removed or renamed, and finding origin/basis snapshots are not admitted. Explicit valid correction may change any permitted non-ID current field without implicitly changing the Review assessment.
Full Review recording and explanation-only updates preserve all complete existing findings, while explicit finding operations follow their own mutable-field rules.

Every existing change-level blocker retains its complete original Origin unchanged throughout its lifetime, including after disposition; current judgments and concern-field edits cannot replace its supporting basis.

Failed evidence, completed activity, historical external-subject drift, or absent optional verification_basis alone does not reject a structurally sound correction. Invalid internal references and failed explicitly declared freshness checks retain their independent rejection or conflict rules.

Recorded roles, matching hashes, supplied judgments, or a successful validation do not establish approval, independence, applicability, or completion. Verify-basis necessity remains a reliance decision at its current owner and is never inferred from prose or treated as a Git instruction.

sources.basis: Derive this draft lower-level obligation from the containing SR at the selected command or operational-record responsibility boundary. Allocation and acceptance criteria are design claims for review, not implementation, requirement approval, or satisfaction evidence.

sources.locator: docs/design/cli/cli.md#CLI-SR-07, CLI-SR-26; docs/design/cli/records.md#RF-SR-03, RF-SR-04, RF-SR-05, RF-SR-08, RF-SR-10, RF-SR-11, RF-SR-13
sources.basis: Preserve the applicable current public and stored-record guarantees at this accountable boundary. The named source retains exact schemas, operation tables, classifications, limits, and historical adoption obligations; this allocation neither replaces those details nor accepts REM authoring JSON as operational records.
